Writing this from the perspective of an animator and not a consumer.
>The #1, biggest problem in my opinion
With the standard corporate industry going down indie has become a funnel for professionals with no job to go into. You notice this with Glitch productions looking at who works there. Everyone is a former industry animator, literal people with families and shit
BUT WHERE DO THE NEW ANIMATORS GO?
I go to art college, I'm constantly hearing shit like make a series, just do it, here's the truth about that:
>#2 problem
You either have money or you don't.
SO many indie series exist that simply don't have money, so they prey on young artists (me) to do free work for them.
My entire, 5+ year experience working as a new animator is, guess what, unpaid labor volunteer projects.
And I'm fed up, okay? You wanna know my issue? What I fucking hate about indie animation? Where do I fucking go to make money? When a project has money, people who worked at fucking CN/WB/whatever take the jobs leaving people like me with free scrap projects, which, more often than not, I join these projects and there's no leadership at all, and things fall apart.
>#3 problem
The big projects? it's all influencers who kow each other.
Does talent even matter anymore? Apparently not. I mean, I know this since I go to art school. I constantly hear that it matters who you know, and that applies online too. But guess what! There are no entry level jobs, there is no indie studio training new animators, so take a moment and guess what that means.
ding ding ding! if you answered: to get into the indie animation industry you have to become a social media influencer, you are correct!
I'm so sick of this. I'm SO sick of job hunting for jobs that don't exist. I'm so sick of applying to things, then getting ghosted, people telling me my work is good, but also apparently not good enough to get hired! How much longer will this go on? Until I'm fucking 30??

item.title: [ 62] Republicans Pay Dweeb $250,000 to Humiliate Himself, Boost El-Sayed
item.description:
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/abdul-el-sayed-heckler

Michigan heckler the son of Republican adviser paid for ‘influencer marketing’ against El-Sayed

Timmy Teepell’s firm paid $250,000 by America Next, which has been trying to gin up ‘organic’ opposition to El-Sayed

The man who attempted to ambush the Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed with a question about his supposed allegiance to the Muslim Brotherhood – which El-Sayed parlayed into a viral clip for his campaign – is the son of a political operator who recently received $250,000 for “canvassing and influencer marketing” against El-Sayed, the Guardian has learned.

In the now-famous exchange, a man – first identified by the Handbasket as Thomas “Tommy” Teepell – asked El-Sayed if he would “disavow” the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed said he would, but then asked: “What are you implying? Do you assume that I wouldn’t?” What followed was a five-minute exchange that has drawn over 50m views across several social media platforms, in which El-Sayed queries the man about the guarantees of religious freedom in the constitution.

Teepell is the son of Timothy “Timmy” Teepell, a longtime strategist for the Missouri Republican senator Josh Hawley as well as former Republican Louisiana governor Bobby Jindal. Timmy Teepell’s firm, Breakthrough LLC, was paid $250,000 on 29 September by America Next, a 501(c)(4) non-profit with which it shares a Baton Rouge office suite, according to a filing with the Federal Election Commission (FEC).

The filing says the money would fund the canvassing and influencer marketing in opposition to El-Sayed. It is the only independent expenditure the group has reported since 2015, when it paid OnMessage Inc for television advertising backing Bobby Jindal’s presidential campaign.

item.title: [ 36] CBS REPORTER DELETES and Apologizes for Blatantly Biased Tweet Smearing Abdul El-Sayed
item.description:
https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/oct/18/cbs-reporter-apologizes-abdul-el-sayed-post

CBS’s chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford has apologized for and deleted a social media post praising a man who questioned the Democratic Michigan US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed about the Muslim Brotherhood during a town hall on Saturday.

On Sunday, Crawford, who initially joined CBS in 2009, wrote on twitter: “Earlier, I tweeted a video from an Abdul El-Sayed town hall. I deleted that tweet because it was a violation of CBS News standards. I apologize.”

Crawford’s deleted post had thanked a man named Tommy, who has been later outed as a Republican operative worked for Republican senator Josh Hawley, while also saying: “I had to watch this twice to catch Dr Abdul El-Sayed’s nanosecond, ‘yeah, absolutely,’ response. His subsequent uninterrupted three-minute diatribe proving your exact point is the kind of spectacular self own most [people] only dream about triggering. Congrats.”

The video to which Crawford referred showed the man who identified himself only as Tommy asking El-Sayed: “Will you disavow the Muslim Brotherhood?”

In response, El-Sayed said: “Sure. Yeah, absolutely. Why are you asking the question?”

Tommy replied: “Well, because they’re a terrorist group.” El-Sayed then rejoined, “But what are you implying? Do you assume that I wouldn’t?

“You’re asking the question because implicitly you assume that I’ll have dual loyalties, right? You assume that somehow I wouldn’t disavow, or that I’ll have some higher order allegiance than the constitution.”

Crawford’s tweet evidently generated substantial backlash from within CBS and among other members of the news media.

The Guardian’s media reporter Jeremy Barr wrote on twitter on Sunday: “I’m told there was a lot of internal backlash at CBS News to the Jan Crawford tweet – which may be why she deleted it.”

item.description:
https://nypost.com/2026/10/18/us-news/air-force-commando-dies-after-falling-from-170-foot-rafters-during-fast-rope-demonstration-at-utsa-game/
An Air Force commando who fell from the 170-foot rafters in front of thousands of horrified fans at a University of Texas at San Antonio football game Saturday has died.

The airman slipped while rappelling from the roof of the Alamodome before the UTSA game against Navy — and plunged to the ground.

The service member, who was assigned to the 6th Combat Training Squadron, Detachment 2, was mortally injured during a pregame demonstration at the school’s “Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans” game.
Videos circulating on social media appeared to show the airman losing control and sliding down the rope during a fast-rope demonstration involving four military personnel.
He received medical treatment on the field for about 10 minutes before being rushed to a local hospital, where he died.

On the field, UTSA staff members formed a semicircle around him before he got pulled away on a stretcher, according to the San Antonio Express-News.

item.title: [ 37] /out/ings with a Pipe Autumn Edition
item.description:
Last thread >>2868475

This is a thread for enjoying a pipe while doing outdoor activities. If you ask why this belongs on /out/, you've never spent
an evening by the campfire with a pipe silently enjoying the nature around you, and you're missing out.

>how to get started
Purchase a corn cob pipe (or a cheap briar pipe) and a pouch of Half and Half or Captain Black tobacco from a smoke shop
or online. You will need a lighter or match, and something to tamp it with--a large nail works well if you don't have a pipe tool.
Fill the pipe with tobacco, pack it down halfway, top it off, pack it down to 3/4, top it off again, pack gently and enjoy. Smoke
slower than you think you need to, the tobacco tastes best when it is burning cool. Tamp and re-light as needed. If you still
have trouble, try different methods on YouTube until you find one that works for you.
>smoking a pipe will give you cancer
Originally the Surgeon General found that pipe and cigar smokers, following a careful study of the statistics (at a time when
most adults smoked, so they had a good sample size), had insignificant death rate increases. Nowadays, tobacco is being
legislated against while hard drugs are being legalized. Put two and two together. Tobacco is just another good thing under attack by the government.

>muh weed
Not the time or place. Start your own thread.

All tobacco users welcome.

item.title: [182] ganja /out/ings
item.description:
This is a thread for enjoying a pipe while doing outdoor activities. If you ask why this belongs on /out/, you've never spent an evening by the campfire with a pipe or bowl or blunt or spliff or joint or vape or edible or dab or oil, silently enjoying the nature around you, and you're missing out.

>How to get started
Purchase a cheap glass pipe (or a simple wooden chillum) and a bag of some quality outdoor or mid-grade weed from a dispensary
or your usual guy. You will need a lighter and something to clear the bowl witha paperclip works well if you don't have a proper tool.
Pack the bowl loosely, enough for airflow but enough to stay lit. Light the corner of the bowl and inhale slow. Smoke
slower than you think you need to, the flower tastes best when it isn't cherried too hot. Tamp and corner or re-light as needed. If you still
have trouble, try different methods on YouTube until you find one that works for you. Or you can just roll it or whatever.

>smoking ganja will get you arrested
Originally, the government found that weed smokers, following a careful study of the statistics (at a time when hemp was a cash crop) were just peaceful people who wanted to grow their own medicine, enjoy jazz and engage in mild tomfoolery. Nowadays, weed is being legalized against while the average American thrashes in the thralls of poverty. Put two and two together. Marijuana is just another good thing that was under attack by the government.

>muh tobacco
Not the time or place (unless you're European.) Start your own thread.

All cannabis users welcome.
